lessons.title: Présenter une camarade
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Introduce a classmate: Say each Spanish vowel clearly: a, e, i, o, u.
lessons.objective: Présentez une nouvelle camarade, reliez son origine à ses études et adaptez la formule de présentation au registre de l’échange.
lessons.coreTie: Reuses Core 1 introductions and Core 11 origin; the source repeats beginner content rather than advancing Master grammar.
lessons.focus: je suis / il est / nous sommes; s’appeler; tu vs vous in introductions

grammar.explanation: French introductions use je suis for identity, venir de or être de for origin, and s’appeler for names: je m’appelle Ana, mon camarade s’appelle Diego. Tu is informal; vous is used with an unfamiliar adult or in a formal setting. Bonjour and enchanté(e) can make a first meeting more polite. French vowels a, e, i, o, u do not follow the Spanish pronunciation rule in the pinned source objective; practise French vowel contrasts separately.

model.origin: Je viens du Pérou et j’étudie la musique.

grammar.caution: The English source teaches Spanish vowel sounds and repeats beginner introductions under Master. This French draft preserves the English sentence meanings, teaches French forms, and flags the stage-placement problem; it does not claim advanced Master progression. “Spanish students” is interpreted as students of Spanish, not students from Spain.

lessons.scene: Elena accueille une nouvelle camarade dans un cours d’espagnol et présente Diego à Ana.
dialogue: Bonjour, je suis Elena.|Hello, I am Elena.
Je viens du Pérou et j’étudie la musique.|I am from Peru and I study music.
Mon camarade s’appelle Diego.|My classmate's name is Diego.
Il vient du Chili.|He is from Chile.
Nous sommes étudiants en espagnol.|We are Spanish students.
Comment tu t’appelles ?|What is your name?
Bonjour !|Hello, good morning.
Je m’appelle Ana.|My name is Ana.
Je suis étudiante.|I am a student.
Comment tu t’appelles ?|What is your name?
Je m’appelle Luis.|My name is Luis.
Enchantée de faire ta connaissance, Luis.|Nice to meet you, Luis.
lessons.speaking: Introduce Elena and Diego to a new classmate, including their origins and Elena’s music studies. Ask the classmate’s name informally, then repeat one greeting with vous for a formal meeting. Clarify that the group studies Spanish; close with a suitable nice-to-meet-you phrase.

words.note: Étudiant is masculine; étudiante feminine.
French bonjour covers both hello and good morning; the two English cards collapse to one natural French greeting.
The written ending of enchanté/enchantée agrees with the speaker; the formal phrase uses votre.
The English source “you call” is a bare gloss; French tu appelles needs an object, e.g. tu appelles Ana.
Me is a clitic; moi-même is the emphatic/reflexive “myself”, not an interchangeable object.
Te is a clitic; toi-même is emphatic/reflexive “yourself”.
French est does not distinguish Spanish ser and estar.

words.fr: Je viens du Pérou et j’étudie la musique.
words.en: I am from Peru and I study music.

words.note: “Spanish students” means students of Spanish in this classroom context, not nationality.

lessons.title: Préparer le premier cours
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Pack for a first class: A noun has grammatical gender.
lessons.objective: Décrivez le matériel nécessaire au cours, localisez-le précisément et distinguez genre grammatical, article et pronom.
lessons.coreTie: Reuses Foundation classroom objects and Core 18 locations; source is beginner-level despite Master placement.
lessons.focus: un/une, le/la/l’; il y a; sur, près de, dans; accord de bleu

grammar.explanation: A French noun has grammatical gender: un livre, une table. The article agrees with the noun, not the owner of the object. Use il y a for there is/are, sur for on a surface, dans for inside a bag, and près de for near. Adjectives may agree in gender: un livre bleu, une sacoche bleue. La can also be a direct-object pronoun before a verb, but here it is mostly an article.

model.need: J’ai besoin d’un sac à dos pour le cours.
model.surface: Le cahier est sur la table.
model.near: La chaise est près de la porte.
model.inside: Je mets le livre dans le sac à dos.

grammar.caution: The source repeats Foundation gender and classroom-object content rather than introducing Master-level structures. French sac à dos is masculine, unlike the Spanish mochila. English “class / classroom” spans cours and salle de classe; the card gives both with context.

lessons.scene: Avant de sortir, deux camarades vérifient le matériel sur la table et dans leur sac.
dialogue: J’ai besoin d’un sac à dos pour le cours.|I need a backpack for class.
Le cahier est sur la table.|The notebook is on the table.
La chaise est près de la porte.|The chair is near the door.
J’ai un livre bleu.|I have a blue book.
Je mets le livre dans le sac à dos.|I put the book in the backpack.
Maintenant, j’ai tout ce qu’il faut pour étudier.|Now I have everything for studying.
Il y a une table dans la salle de classe.|There is a table in the classroom.
Le livre est sur la table.|The book is on the table.
J’ai un cahier et un sac à dos.|I have a notebook and a backpack.
Le sac à dos est bleu.|The backpack is blue.
J’ai besoin d’une chaise.|I need a chair.
La chaise est ici.|The chair is here.
lessons.speaking: Pack for the first class. Tell a classmate what you need and where the notebook, chair, book and backpack are. Ask them to locate one item, correct a mistaken location with sur/dans/près de, then confirm that you have everything needed.

words.note: Sac à dos is masculine in French.
Cours is a class/session; salle de classe is the room. The source gloss covers both.
French est covers identity, condition and location; there is no ser/estar split.
Se trouve explicitly locates something; est also works.
Il y a works for singular and plural “there is/are”.
La can be a feminine article or an object pronoun.
Un is a masculine article; une is feminine.

lessons.title: Préparer le matériel du groupe
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Prepare materials for a group: Usually add -s after a vowel and -es after a consonant.
lessons.objective: Comptez et répartissez le matériel du groupe en accordant articles, noms et adjectifs au pluriel.
lessons.coreTie: Reuses Core 14 plural forms and Core 24 recipients; source is a beginner inventory rather than a Master-level task.
lessons.focus: un/une → des; le/la → les; plural -s, -x and irregular forms; il y a

grammar.explanation: French plural articles become les or des: le livre → les livres, une chaise → des chaises. Most nouns add written -s; many -eau nouns take -x (un tableau → des tableaux), and some plurals are irregular. The final consonant is often silent, but an article may link to the noun in speech. Use il y a with either singular or plural. For a group, distinguish what is on the table from what is still needed.

model.group: Il y a quatre étudiants dans le groupe.
model.shortage: Il n’y a que deux livres sur la table.
model.bags: Les sacs à dos sont sous les chaises.

grammar.caution: The pinned Spanish objective says add -s after a vowel and -es after a consonant, which is not a French plural rule. This French draft teaches French spelling instead. The source repeats Foundation plural/inventory content under Master; curriculum progression needs redesign before release.

lessons.scene: Quatre camarades comptent livres, cahiers et crayons avant de commencer le cours.
dialogue: Il y a quatre étudiants dans le groupe.|There are four students in the group.
Il nous faut quatre livres.|We need four books.
Il n’y a que deux livres sur la table.|There are only two books on the table.
Ana apporte deux cahiers.|Ana brings two notebooks.
Les sacs à dos sont sous les chaises.|The backpacks are under the chairs.
Les crayons sont près des cahiers.|The pencils are near the notebooks.
J’ai deux livres.|I have two books.
Les livres sont pour le cours.|The books are for the class.
Il y a trois cahiers sur la table.|There are three notebooks on the table.
Les chaises sont ici.|The chairs are here.
Il nous faut deux crayons.|We need two pencils.
Les crayons sont dans le sac à dos.|The pencils are in the backpack.
lessons.speaking: Prepare materials for four classmates. Count the books, notebooks and pencils; identify what is on the table, under the chairs and inside the backpack. Tell your partner what is missing, ask them to bring it, and confirm each plural quantity.

words.note: Sac à dos is masculine; its plural is sacs à dos.
Cours is a class/session; salle de classe is the room.
Il y a works for singular and plural.
La is a feminine article or object pronoun by context.
Choose dans, sur or à by place meaning; the source English gloss is broad.
French sont covers identity, condition and location; there is no ser/estar split.
Se trouvent highlights location; sont can also locate objects.
Les is plural regardless of gender; it may also be an object pronoun.
